interface_detail: SSH on port 22; an SSH public key is registered with the provisioning API
chaining: a keepalive file is the cheapest way past the sweep, and it costs one touch

free_tier.stated: a free shared shell account; per-user limits applied at login are 512 MB memory, 50% CPU quota and a soft 150 process cap
free_tier.notes: the limits live in the operator's deployed configuration, not on a marketing page

retention.stated: a daily sweep terminates sessions for any user with no SSH login in 30 days unless ~/.keep-account exists
retention.notes: the sweep keys off lastlog, so a detached tmux does not keep it alive

limits.value: sessions terminated after 30 days with no SSH login unless ~/.keep-account exists
512 MB memory, 50% CPU quota, soft 150 and hard 200 processes per user at login
an SSH public key must be registered with the provisioning API

identity_cost.detail: an account with a registered SSH key; no card

evidence.proved: TCP connect succeeded in 0.35 s to 174.138.102.152; the host accepted the connection and sent no banner within 6 s
the daily clean-lurkers script sets DAYS=30 and runs lastlog -b 30 -t 32 to terminate users with no login in 30 days

notes: The 30-day sweep is the only real constraint and it has a one-file opt-out. An earlier seed revision said there was no purge cron; that was wrong, and the cron lives outside /etc/crontab.

persistent_storage.max_retention: 30 days without a login unless opted out

confidence_note: reachability only: a probe proves the port answers, not the quota, so the per-user limits carry the documented rung and the record is not `measured`
binding_note: the 30-day login sweep binds first, with a one-file opt-out
